title: An image is a number array
summary: OpenCV is a library for working with images. A small colour image can be stored as rows, columns and three colour values per pixel.
introduction: OpenCV is a library for working with images. A small colour image can be stored as rows, columns and three colour values per pixel. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain an image is a number array
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: OpenCV is a library for working with images. A small colour image can be stored as rows, columns and three colour values per pixel.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.text: Use Python with numpy and opencv-python-headless installed in a separate local environment. No camera or network is used. These examples do not run in the browser playground.
This course teaches the basics. It does not cover every feature of OpenCV. Keep real personal data and secret keys out of practice files.

blocks.code:
import cv2
import numpy as np

image = np.zeros((3, 4, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
print(image.shape)
blocks.title: An image is a number array

blocks.text: The output is (3, 4, 3). There are three rows, four columns and three colour channels. zeros makes a black image with every value equal to zero.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Create an image with two rows and five columns.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Array shape lists height before width; mixing them up swaps the intended picture size.
For more detail later, use this [OpenCV further reading](https://docs.opencv.org/4.x/d6/d00/tutorial_py_root.html).
